newsitem.title: GERMANY: German GDP grows 1.5 pct in Apr-June 1996 from Q1.
newsitem.headline: German GDP grows 1.5 pct in Apr-June 1996 from Q1.

text.p: The German economy showed a strong 1.5 percent growth rebound in the second quarter from the previous quarter, when it had shrunk 0.5 percent, the Federal Statistics Office said on Thursday.
Measured against the year-earlier quarter, gross domestic product grew 1.2 percent in the second quarter, up from 0.2 percent year-on-year growth in the first quarter.
Uwe Angenendt of BHF Bank told Reuters Financial Television the second-quarter growth figures were "on the upper end of expecations. It is quite good news for the German economy".

Economist Mathias Hafner of BZW said, "The numbers are good but we believe that growth will normalise in the second half of the year and give the Bundesbank little reason to do anything else on interest rates. For the second half we expect more moderate growth, around 0.5 percent on the quarter."
West Germany showed growth of 1.0 percent in the second quarter from the previous quarter, according to the Economics Ministry, and 1.1 percent from the year-earlier quarter.
The east German economy grew a vigorous 5.0 percent from the previous quarter, and 2.6 percent from the year-earlier period.
Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said 1996 growth could be stronger than previous government expectations. His ministry in April forecast that growth for the full year would be 0.75 percent.
"An increasing number of economic indicators speak for a continuation of the economic revival," Rexrodt said.
Private consumption gained 1.2 percent from a year earlier, while public consumption gained 3.6 percent. Capital investment gained 0.5 percent, but construction fell 1.4 percent.
Exports gained 2.5 percent and imports fell 0.7 percent.
